system_description: An intelligent, local Google Forms automation studio that scans form structures, configures custom Likert and text data pools, algorithmically extrapolates sample response patterns, and executes automated submissions with humanized variable delay intervals.
deployment_mode: 100% Local (runs on http://127.0.0.1:5000 with Python Flask, no cloud deployment required)

google_form_requirements: The Google Form MUST be public (accessible to anyone with the link).
'Limit to 1 response' in Google Form settings MUST be turned OFF (turning this on requires Google account login, which blocks direct automated submissions).
'Restrict to users in [Organization]' MUST be turned OFF.
The form should not have CAPTCHA plugins or account login walls.
supported_url_formats: https://forms.gle/... (shortened links are automatically followed and resolved)

step_1_connect_and_scan.function: Scans Google Form structure automatically by reading the page and extracting Google's embedded FB_PUBLIC_LOAD_DATA_ object.
extracted_data: Sections count and pageHistory navigation string (e.g., '0,1,2,3')
Question entry IDs (entry.XXXXXXXX), question titles, descriptions, and types
Multiple-Choice Grid evaluation rows and scale options (1 to 5, or descriptive)
step_1_connect_and_scan.fallback: Allows raw HTML source pasting if local network restricts direct scraping.

step_2_configure_and_scale.target_respondents: User inputs desired total respondents (e.g. 50, 100, etc.).

text_pools_shuffling.purpose: Used for typed text questions like College Department.
text_pools_shuffling.behavior: User defines variation tags (e.g., 'COT', 'College of Technologies', 'COB', 'College of Business', 'CAS', etc.). The system randomly and evenly distributes these across respondents so answers never appear repetitive.

likert_scale_and_grid_scaling.purpose: Allows user to provide sample distribution counts for each rating (e.g., 2 for '5', 3 for '4', 1 for '3').
likert_scale_and_grid_scaling.sample_vs_target_logic: If user provides only a small sample (e.g. total 6 sample answers) and requests 50 respondents, the system detects this and triggers the Pattern Scaling Confirmation Modal.
likert_scale_and_grid_scaling.mathematical_algorithm: Uses the Largest Remainder Method (Hare-Niemeyer Algorithm). Proportions of user's sample choices are calculated. Ratings not picked by user (e.g. 1 and 2) remain strictly at 0%. Proportions are scaled to target respondents so the integer sum matches exactly.
likert_scale_and_grid_scaling.anti_streak_shuffling: All generated ratings are globally shuffled across respondents to ensure no continuous, predictable, or robotic streaks exist in the survey submission.

variable_time_intervals.purpose: Simulates natural human respondent timing gaps instead of robotically submitting all responses at once.
variable_time_intervals.configuration: User can add custom delay rules (e.g., 5 min -> 2 respondents, 2 min -> 3 respondents, 30 sec -> 1 respondent).
variable_time_intervals.scaling_and_jitter: Delay rules are proportionally scaled to match total gap intervals (target_respondents - 1), shuffled randomly, and given ±4% human jitter so no two delays are identical.

step_3_preview_and_verify.tabular_preview: Displays the complete generated respondent dataset table before submitting anything.
step_3_preview_and_verify.re_shuffle: Allows user to re-randomize the dataset order with a single click.
step_3_preview_and_verify.export: Allows downloading the dataset plan as a JSON file.

step_4_live_execution.progress_tracking: Displays real-time progress bar, percentage, successful count, failed count, and remaining count.
step_4_live_execution.countdown_timer: Displays a live MM:SS countdown banner showing the remaining sleep time before the next respondent is submitted.
step_4_live_execution.controls: Live Pause, Resume, and Stop/Abort buttons with sub-second responsiveness (sleeps in 0.3s interruptible ticks).
completion_actions: Re-Run Automation: Restarts submission with 1 click.
Change Rating / Responses: Returns to Step 2 to edit Likert ratings, text pools, delays, or respondent counts.
Home / Connect New Form: Returns to Step 1 to scan a new Google Form.

troubleshooting_and_common_errors.http_404_not_found: Occurs if the URL query parameter was malformed or the form is deleted/private. Ensure the link is copied from 'Send' -> 'Link' tab in Google Forms.
troubleshooting_and_common_errors.sign_in_required_or_permission_denied: Occurs when 'Limit to 1 response' or organization domain restriction is turned on in Google Forms settings. Must be toggled off by the form owner.
troubleshooting_and_common_errors.timestamp_in_google_sheets: Google Form generates server-side timestamps upon HTTP arrival. To change timestamps to past dates/weeks for thesis/academic reporting, modify Column A in the linked Google Sheet (e.g. using the provided Google Apps Script in README).

technical_stack.frameworks: Flask (REST API server), Tailwind CSS (UI styling)
technical_stack.http_handling: Requests library with isolated connections (Connection: close) and dual connect/read timeouts to prevent keep-alive socket hanging.
